name: gate-card
description:
The human gate — where an autonomous process stops and asks. The app calls it HITL and it is the most consequential shape in the estate: the one interface where a person takes responsibility for what a machine is about to do.

Two things in the original carry that weight and I had lost both by writing the unit from its class names rather than its render. The border is 2px MARINE, not a tint — this card is meant to stop the eye in a scrolling log, and a soft accent wash does the opposite. And the action lives in a marine FOOTER BAR across the bottom, inverted: a light pill on a dark ground, which is the only place the gate opens. Putting the buttons in a plain row made it look like any other card with two buttons.

The rule underneath: the preview of what will happen is in the same card as the action. An approve button whose consequence is on another screen is a signature on a blank page.

base.$description:
The SAME construction a button wears — a 1px edge and a 4px ring standing off the page — at card scale and in the card's own marine. Not decoration borrowed from the button: a button is the shape that says 'press me', and this is the one card in the system that exists to be pressed, so it should read as the same family. In the button's literal grey (`primary-edge` / `primary-ring`, which are tuned to sit AROUND a dark marine fill) the ring lands on a cream body as a soft shadow and the card stops stopping the eye — so the ring is the marine at 14%, which is the button's language in this card's colour. It replaces a bare 2px border and a coloured drop shadow.

CONTAINER. This unit establishes an inline-size container named after itself, so anything inside it can respond to the width of THIS BOX rather than to the width of the window. That is the difference that matters for a design system: a composite dropped into a 320px sidebar and the same composite on a 320px phone are the same situation, and a viewport query calls them different ones. The library carries no viewport media query anywhere for exactly this reason — the only `@media` in it is `prefers-reduced-motion`, which is a person's setting and not a size.

question.$description: The ask, in one sentence, in the imperative of what YOU are deciding — not 'Gate 4 pending'. A gate whose question is a status line is a gate nobody can answer without opening something else.

asked.$description: Composes `text--mono-meta`. The face comes from the one definition.

preview.$description: WHAT WILL HAPPEN, shown rather than described — on its own white ground inside the card, so it reads as the artefact and not as more of the card's copy. `white-space: pre-wrap` because a draft's line breaks are part of the draft.

actions.$description: A marine bar across the bottom — the only place the gate opens. Full-bleed, which `overflow: hidden` on the card makes possible without negative margins, and the action inside it is INVERTED: a light pill on a dark ground. In a plain row this card looked like any other card with two buttons; the bar is what says a decision is required here. The way out first, the commit last. The block padding is `comfortable`, not `tight`: against a 2.5rem pill the tight value left about four pixels of ground above and below, so the buttons read as cropped by the bar rather than seated in it.

kind.$description: Composes `badge badge--face-mono badge--tone-progress`. It was a hand-built mono pill; the shape, the tint and the ink all belong to `badge`, and only the placement is this unit's.

weight.$description: How much is at stake, which decides how hard the card is to skim past.

routine.$description: A confirmation the answer to which is almost always yes. It drops the ring entirely — a quiet gate that still stands off the page is a gate crying wolf, and the whole point of this weight is not training the eye to click through.

grave.$description: Irreversible — money moving, data deleted, a message sent to a customer. The commit here wears `btn--danger` regardless of whether the action sounds destructive, because irreversible IS the destructive property.

a11y.note: `role=group` named by the question, so a screen reader reaching the buttons has the question as their context rather than two bare verbs. The preview is inside the group for the same reason. A pending gate is announced ONCE via a live region when it appears — not polled, and not silent: a decision waiting where nobody is looking is a stalled process. Never auto-focus the approve button: focus goes to the card, and the person moves to the answer themselves.
